answer: A strong defense is a collateralized identity bond with correlated-behavior slashing. Each agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed when several identities act in lockstep, voting identically or moving funds along the same horizon of transactions. A single fake is cheap, but a violet-flagged cluster that mirrors every move loses all its bonds at once, so the attacker pays per identity multiplied by the cluster penalty. Like yarrow spreading by runners, each new shoot must fund its own bond, and coordinated shoots get cut together.
